solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One taking advantage of work somewhere in Africa in harbour

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work

indicators.note: in says one place name goes inside the word for harbour

parts.note: a port is a harbour
Tunis is the capital of Tunisia, in North Africa

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a job in an African harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One taking advantage' is the definition; 'work' is the abbreviation for opus, not labour.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunist is someone who exploits chances for gain, regardless of principle.

clue.text: Basically fussy and really regularly ignored

parts.note: prim means prudish or fussy

indicators.note: every other letter of really is skipped, keeping the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone is fussy and their fussiness is regularly ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops R, A and L from really, leaving its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean fundamentally or in the first instance, as synonyms.

clue.text: Honour nice as alternative for respect

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: an alternative form of the words nice as means their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Being honoured is offered as a nice substitute for being respected.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a show of deference or respect, such as a bow.

clue.text: Invite violent commotion seeing off bridge opponents

indicators.note: seeing off means getting rid of, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a tempest is a violent storm or uproar
East and South are opposing seats at the bridge table

explanation.surface: An invitation leads to a violent row that drives the bridge opponents away.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt fate or trouble is to invite it; both mean to provoke or court.

clue.text: Figure coming up with metal good for mesh

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A number comes up alongside a good metal suited to making mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Netting is a mesh of knotted cord or wire, the material of a net.

clue.text: Cor! Pet possibly disappears in milling waste products such as this

definitions.text: Cor! Pet possibly disappears in milling waste products such as this

indicators.note: milling means churning around, so the letters of waste products are mixed up
possibly says Cor and Pet may appear in any order of their letters
disappears in says those letters vanish from inside the mixed-up phrase

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a pet animal vanishes into the mill's leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of waste products, remove C, O, R, P, E and T, and the rest rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine wood particles are a waste by-product of sawing timber in a mill.

clue.text: Some international clubs yearn to bag one player

indicators.note: to bag means to capture, so the pieces hold the numeral inside

parts.note: part means some of something
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to pant for something is to yearn for it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: International sports clubs long to sign a particular player.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral sits between PARTIC and PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A participant is one taking part, as a player does in a game.

clue.text: Stumble from topless bar; felt drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about into a new order
topless says the word bar loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles out of a topless bar, feeling drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves AR from bar, and 'drunk' rearranges AR with FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter is to waver or lose one's footing, a synonym for stumbling.

clue.text: Greed is a sin holding soldiers back

indicators.note: holding means the word for sin wraps around the soldiers

parts.note: a vice is a sin

indicators.note: back says RA is read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A statement that greed is a sin holding soldiers back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RA, the Royal Artillery, to AR; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Cut sandwiches to music from America

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between its two halves

parts.note: mown means cut, as grass is

explanation.surface: Sandwiches are cut up to the sound of American music.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the Detroit record label and soul-pop style it gave its name to.

clue.text: Ruin predicted in trouble with EU

indicators.note: in trouble suggests a disordered state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news-style prediction that ruin awaits a troubled European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepitude is a state of decay and dilapidation, a ruinous condition.

clue.text: Swimmers on near edge of treacherous rocks

indicators.note: on means placed after, in an across clue the swimmers come after the edge letter
the near edge of a word is its first letter

parts.note: otters are swimming animals

explanation.surface: Swimming animals are close to the edge of dangerous rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun in the scene; it is the verb, meaning sways.
explanation.definitionFit: Totters and rocks both mean sways unsteadily back and forth.

clue.text: Almost completed short step saving energy payment

indicators.note: almost completed means the word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a short quick step, as in tripping lightly
saving can mean except, as but does
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A building project nearly done saves energy by short steps, costing a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like conserving, but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute was a payment made by one ruler or state to another as a sign of submission.

clue.text: Comedian with variable range

parts.note: Jimmy Carr is a British stand-up comedian
Y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A comedian whose material varies in range.
explanation.definitionFit: The carry of a gun or golf shot is how far it travels, its range.

clue.text: Aggravation at sea losing a good sailor

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up
losing says some letters are lost from the mixed-up word

explanation.surface: Annoyance at sea causes a good sailor to be lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and G away from aggravation and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator is a sailor who plots a ship's course.

clue.text: Clothing I left dropped in dirty room

parts.note: a vest is an item of clothing, an undergarment in Britain

indicators.note: dropped means the letter moves one place lower in this down entry

parts.note: blue means smutty or dirty, as in a blue joke

explanation.surface: Clothing left dropped on the floor of a dirty room.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'dropped' moves the L of BLUE one place down, giving BULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestibule is an entrance hall or lobby, a small room inside a front door.

clue.text: They gas snakes after beginning to panic

indicators.note: after says the snakes come later, following the opening letter of panic
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rattlers is a familiar name for rattlesnakes

explanation.surface: Panic as someone gasses snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like poisoning, but means chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter idly, so those who do it are idle talkers.

clue.text: Unfavourable publicity almost sure to be heartless

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an advert is a piece of publicity

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of sure are removed

explanation.surface: Bad publicity is almost certain to be cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means harmful or contrary, a synonym of unfavourable.

clue.text: Recordings made of time with friends

parts.note: allies are friends or supporters

explanation.surface: Recordings made of time spent with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallies are counts or records kept, as of a score.

clue.text: Organisation in which one is made victim

definitions.meaning: a structure or arrangement, how something is put together

definitions.text: in which one is made victim
definitions.meaning: a frame-up or trap, in which an innocent person is deliberately made to look guilty

explanation.surface: An organisation in which one person is turned into a victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is both an arrangement of parts and a scheme to frame someone.

clue.text: Very fine screen is most weak

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to screen is to test, as for a disease

explanation.surface: A very fine screen is the feeblest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very fine screen' reads as a mesh; it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft can mean weak or feeble, so the superlative means weakest.

clue.text: Degrees ending in success?

parts.note: read as two words; it also names the lowest class of UK honours degree

explanation.surface: Wondering whether university qualifications lead to success.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as THIRD S, it describes the last letter of success, its third S. A third is the lowest class of British honours degree, hardly a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-class degrees are the lowest classification of a British bachelor's honours result.

clue.text: Composition of two foreign articles after a month

indicators.note: after says the pair of articles follows the month abbreviation

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November
el and la are the Spanish and French/Spanish words for the

explanation.surface: A piece of music made of two overseas articles written a month on.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a written composition, a short novel.

clue.text: Divine gold carpet going upwards

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: in a down entry going upwards means read in reverse

parts.note: a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A sacred golden carpet rising into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foretell or predict, as divining does.

clue.text: Deliver case of iron and copper in Nice and lead in Toulouse

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside pair of letters

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer, a copper in Nice

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shipping iron and copper casings to Nice and lead to Toulouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' and 'lead' look like metals with iron; copper is a policeman, lead the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflict a blow or penalty is to deliver it.

clue.text: Lamentable being pregnant after a Romeo disappears

indicators.note: disappears says those letters go missing from the longer word

parts.note: carrying a child means being pregnant
Romeo is R in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A sad tale of pregnancy after a lover vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying, as in a crying shame, means deplorable or lamentable.

clue.text: Capsized over and over

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in time is up
ended means over or finished

explanation.surface: A boat that turned over and over again.
explanation.definitionFit: Upended means turned upside down, as a capsized boat is.

clue.text: Aboard ship, peer as net entangled marine monsters

indicators.note: aboard means put on a ship, so the mixed letters go inside SS

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: entangled means twisted together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: On deck, a sailor peers as a net gets tangled with sea monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea serpents are legendary giant snake-like creatures of the ocean.
